## Natural history notes

A pale, shrubby reindeer lichen characterized by finely branched, gray-white to yellowish-gray tufts that form soft mats or cushions on the ground. In Florida, it is found in dry, sandy, nutrient-poor habitats such as scrub, sandhills, pine flatwoods, open pinewoods, and disturbed sandy areas where light reaches the soil surface. Like other lichens, it is a symbiotic association between a fungus and photosynthetic partner, helping colonize exposed sandy substrates while absorbing moisture and nutrients from the air rather than feeding on plants.
